description:
Most space stories honor the people who flew. We turned to the machines that stayed: rovers, landers and helicopters that fell silent after the headlines moved on. Using NASA mission records, we built a game where they speak first.

Philip Treasure Oluwadurotimi, Project Lead, Content Developer & Video Editor (Nigeria): led the team, wrote the stories, edited the demo.

Favour Boluwatife Philip, Software Engineer (Nigeria): designed, built, tested and hosted the game.
summary:
Last Signal is a free web game and interactive story about the machines NASA left behind on the Moon and Mars. Players become Signal Operators: they tune a radio dial to a glowing signal on a 3D Moon or Mars, listen as the machine tells its own story in the first person, then decode what they heard with questions and an ordering round. Each success earns a mission patch, stars, points and a rank, and unlocks the full story at three reading levels (Kids, Explorer, Scientist), a timeline replay, and "Ask about my mission", a chat that answers only from the machine's own sourced fact file and honestly refuses everything else.

Fifteen machines are included, from Surveyor 3, the Apollo rovers and lunar modules to Spirit, Opportunity, Viking, Phoenix, InSight and Ingenuity. One is not silent: the Apollo 11 laser mirror, still used by scientists today. Every date, number and place is matched to the NASA sources listed in the app.

It installs like an app, works offline after the first visit, and supports captions, voices, keyboard play and reduced motion, so it reaches classrooms with poor connections. Abandoned, but not forgotten.
details:
LAST SIGNAL: Stories from the silent machines

Live URL: https://last-signal-nasa-challenge2026.vercel.app

Github Repository: https://github.com/philipfavourboluwatife247/last-signal-nasa-challenge2026.git

Team: Last Signal

WHAT IT DOES

Last Signal is a web game and interactive story that tells the stories of NASA's discarded machines on the Moon and Mars to school-age space fans. You are a Signal Operator. Fifteen glowing signals sit at the real coordinates of machines on a 3D Moon and Mars, from Surveyor 3 and the Apollo rovers and lunar modules to Spirit, Opportunity, Viking 1 and 2, Phoenix, InSight and Ingenuity. One machine is still working: the Apollo 11 laser mirror, which scientists still use today.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Tune: slide a radio dial until static clears to a tone.

2. Listen: the machine tells its own story in the first person, typed, captioned and spoken.

3. Decode: questions answerable from what you just heard, plus an ordering round for timelines.

4. Reward: a mission patch, stars, points and a rank from Cadet to Legend.

5. Unlock: the full story at three levels (Kids, Explorer, Scientist), a mission replay with true elapsed time, and "Ask about my mission".

Around this: planets and the Sun to tap, shooting stars to catch, a daily signal, a Mission Log, and a microphone feature that echoes your voice across space (processed on the device, never uploaded).

WHY IT IS DIFFERENT

- Learn first, then quiz. A newcomer is never tested on something they have not heard.

- Honest by design. "Ask about my mission" is not a generative chatbot. It retrieves answers only from the machine's own fact file, shows its sources, and says so when it does not know. It cannot invent facts.

- Accuracy you can inspect. Each machine is one data file with sourced key numbers. A validator fails the build on bad data. Every claim is listed with its NASA source on the in-app Credits page and in docs/FACT_CHECK.md. Each NASA photo is labelled as a photo from the surface, a model on Earth, or an artist's concept.

INTENDED IMPACT

The machines NASA left behind are usually told in dense technical pages. Last Signal turns them into a story a student, explorers and scientists can play in minutes. It installs like an app, works offline after the first visit, uses self-hosted fonts and no accounts, and saves progress only on the device. Because every story is a data file, it grows with NASA's data: adding a machine means adding one file, not rebuilding the game.

ACCESSIBILITY

Captions for all spoken text, separate voice switch, keyboard play, native slider for tuning, reduced-motion support, quality tiers for slow phones, and a full-screen photo viewer. Automated axe-core checks (WCAG 2.x A and AA) found no violations on the screens tested. We recommend, and have not yet done, a manual screen-reader pass.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY

Next.js 14, React 18 and TypeScript. 3D with three.js, React Three Fiber and custom GLSL shaders (surfaces, signal rings and impacts are painted in the shader). GSAP for camera motion, Zustand for state, Tailwind CSS, zod for the data schema. Sound is generated in code with the Web Audio API; spoken lines use the browser's text-to-speech; speech recognition and MediaRecorder power spoken answers and the voice echo. Hand-written service worker for offline use. Hosted on Vercel; source on GitHub.

QUALITY CHECKS

npm run build runs a content validator, schema tests, and 63 automated test questions for the Ask engine (right answers, and refusal of off-topic questions) before every build.

HONEST LIMITS

Speech and voices depend on the player's browser.
